title: Shape the Fusion workspace
question: Choose the structure that should guide the redesign. Every option keeps your neutral palette, restrained glass, readable type, responsive behavior, and performance constraints.

options.label: Tabbed evidence folio
options.lineage: tabbed reference manuals and punched acetate overlays
options.thesis: A clear, tabbed reading surface keeps each project stage and its source trail easy to follow.
materials: restrained translucent navigation over solid reading surfaces
Fusion jade for active evidence links
options.viewport: The project title and next action sit above a visible seven-stage workflow. A pending source conflict leads the page; requirements and sources continue in one shared reading grid.
options.risk: If every surface is translucent, quotations lose contrast and the workspace feels like a physical-book costume.

raised.raise: High-consequence choices stay apart from nearby actions, with a clear focus boundary and rationale before they are recorded.

options.label: Cited delivery brief
options.lineage: consulting decision briefs with a compact citation apparatus
options.thesis: Start with the question a delivery lead must answer, then keep the source trail beside it.
options.viewport: A single open decision occupies the main reading column, with its two source statements and impact. A narrow context rail holds project status and linked requirements; the register follows below.
options.risk: This is the most familiar direction and can become a conventional project dashboard if the evidence trail stops leading.

options.label: Seven-stage source wallet
options.lineage: jet-age ticket wallets and their retained journey stubs
options.thesis: The workflow reads as a visible sequence; completed and unresolved stages remain in place.
materials: folded process sequence translated into tabs
options.viewport: The seven project stages form a numbered rail. Selecting a stage opens its evidence or review surface, while pending work remains visibly marked in the sequence.
options.case: Competitive: the sequence clarifies where work stands and preserves state; the travel reference identifies less with the delivery lead.
options.risk: The ticket form feels playful if process names and decision states are reduced to decoration.

options.label: Layered reference manual
options.lineage: boxed-software manuals with transparent acetate leaves and a stepped tab rail
options.thesis: One active section lifts above a transparent layer while supporting text stays on a clear reading surface.
materials: neutral section board translated to one restrained Fusion accent
options.viewport: A seven-tab rail names Overview, Requirements, Evidence, Conflicts, Decisions, Ask Fusion, and BRD. The selected section opens as a high-contrast page with traceable references.
options.case: Competitive: section tabs fit the product's workflow; the manual's single-size typography and multicolor boards weaken information hierarchy and the neutral brief.
options.risk: Literal manual details can make the interface feel like a book instead of a responsive workspace.

regions.label: active section title and next action
opaque reading page with evidence links

options.label: Evidence grid
options.lineage: Wim Crouwel's cell-built type specimens and visible construction grids
options.thesis: A stable grid makes requirement IDs, confidence, state, and source references easy to compare.
options.viewport: A consistent twelve-column ledger carries the project title, process rail, pending decision, and priority requirements. Columns collapse into labeled records on narrow screens.
options.case: Competitive: the grid improves comparison and alignment; the original typographic specimen does not naturally identify a delivery review.
options.risk: A visible grid can overpower the content if every field is boxed.

options.label: Dark-first developer console
options.lineage: graphite developer consoles divided by hairline seams
options.thesis: A compact panel system isolates high-consequence actions and gives each state one restrained accent.
options.viewport: The project opens with a fixed left rail and a dense panel layout for status, source comparison, and action controls.
options.case: Declined: the developer-console audience and dark panel field conflict with the consultant's evidence review and the requested restrained glass system.
options.kept: Separate consequential choices from neighboring actions, with visible focus and a clear rationale before saving.
options.risk: Panel density can hide the source trail and make the interface feel technical rather than consultative.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A conventional project workspace keeps navigation, current status, an open decision, and the requirements register in familiar order.
canonCard.viewport: A plain project header and seven-stage process line lead into one pending-decision area and a requirements table, without a decorative card grid.
canonCard.risk: Familiar by design; it offers less character than the other directions.
